app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98 — unsubscribe mutates state (notification level) on a GET with check_xhr skipped, so email clients, link scanners, and prefetchers will unsubscribe/mute users without a click; it also lacks CSRF protection, enabling attacks; should be a confirm page with a PUT/POST action

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action that **changes state** (`tu.notification_level` is modified and `tu.save!`) and exposes it via **GET routes** (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`). It also explicitly skips the `check_xhr` filter for `:unsubscribe`, making it callable as a normal browser GET. Because it’s a GET that mutates user state and relies on the user’s session cookie, it is susceptible to unintended triggering by link prefetchers/scanners and to CSRF-style triggering from third-party pages (e.g., an `` hit in a logged-in browser). The finding matches what is verifiably present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — Writing notification_level directly and calling save! bypasses TopicUser.change, so notifications_reason_id/notifications_changed_at are not set and no notification_level_change MessageBus event is published, leaving other clients out of sync and UI reason text wrong

adjudication.rationale: In the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action, the code fetches a `TopicUser` record, mutates `tu.notification_level`, and calls `tu.save!` directly. Elsewhere in this codebase (see `TopicUser.change` in the diff), notification level updates are expected to go through `TopicUser.change`, which explicitly publishes a `MessageBus` `notification_level_change` event when `attrs[:notification_level]` is present and may also be responsible for any ancillary bookkeeping tied to that pathway. Because `unsubscribe` bypasses `TopicUser.change`, no `MessageBus` event will be published from this update path, so other open clients won’t be notified of the change. The claim about specific fields like `notifications_reason_id/notifications_changed_at` can’t be directly verified from the diff, but the “bypasses `TopicUser.change` so no publish / bookkeeping” core issue is real and verifiable.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action and adds `unsubscribe_url` into email templating, but the proposed finding is about missing specs/coverage rather than a concrete bug or defect in the code. The absence of new controller/mailer specs is not a verifiable correctness/security problem in the diff itself. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3 — Template is at topic/unsubscribe while the route is top-level topicUnsubscribe; the resolver may map to topic-unsubscribe/topic_unsubscribe rather than the nested path, so the page may render blank; verify resolver mapping or rename the file

adjudication.rationale: In the diff the Ember route is defined as a top-level `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', ...)`, which will conventionally resolve to `topic-unsubscribe` (dasherized) for its template/controller/view. That matches the added files `controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` and `views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`. However, the template was added at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which corresponds to a nested route name like `topic.unsubscribe` (dot-notation), not `topicUnsubscribe`. With this mismatch, Ember/Discourse is likely to not find the intended template for the route and render the wrong template/blank outlet.
